title: On the minimal cycle lengths of the Collatz sequences
status: read (PDF from the probleme-syracuse.fr mirror; undated preprint, University of Oulu, listed as entry 105 of Lagarias's annotated bibliography II as 2003+)
notes: Registered 20 September 2026, when Philippe asked for a published 3x-1 verification floor and this turned up instead. THE PAPER. Lemma 1 (3x+1) and Lemma 6 (3x-1): if a nontrivial cycle of length m = n + k, with n halvings and k odd steps, has least element above R, then n/k lies between log2(3 - 1/R) and log2 3 on the 3x-1 side, so n/k is a best lower rational approximation of log2 3. Table 2 lists those approximations with the cycle length m = n + k and the bound R = 1/(3 - 2^(n/k)) 'to be reached by computer calculations or by theoretical studies to eliminate the possibility of cycle of this size to exist'. WHAT IT IS FOR THIS LABORATORY. Table 2 IS the negative-cycle survivor table of J-negative-cycle-finance-is-the-juggler-mirror and Paper A's Remark 5.20: the same lengths, our K being his n and our o his k, and his R for our rows reproduced here to five digits (K = 9538065, o = 6017849: 1.25334e12 against his 1.25335e12; K = 16483927: 2.96789e13; K = 4404167: 3.43420e11). His bound is the Crandall-type multiplier bound; ours is the even-charge finance, which is sharper by one or two rows at each floor: at 2^38 his smallest surviving length is 3800179 against our 4404167, at 2^40 it is 9236071 against 9538065, at 2^44 it is 16181933 against 16483927. So the conditional table was in print, in his form, in 2003. What is ours is the sharper constant, the kernel-checked implication neg_cycle_finance, and now the floors themselves. WHAT IT DOES NOT GIVE. No verified floor for 3x-1: the last column is framed as a target for computation, and he reports none. On the positive side he gets a minimal 3x+1 cycle length of at least 630,138,897 from Oliveira e Silva's 2.70e16 (Lagarias's wording). CITATION GAP. Neither literature/ nor docs/ mentioned Sinisalo before today. Paper A's Remark 5.20 cites him since its revision of 20 September 2026.
